definitions.explanation: The person who conducts an interview, typically in job recruitment or academic admissions contexts.

examples.japanese: {面接官|めんせつかん}に{質問|しつもん}された。
examples.english: I was asked a question by the interviewer.

examples.japanese: {面接官|めんせつかん}の{印象|いんしょう}はとても{良|よ}かった。
examples.english: The impression of the interviewer was very good.

examples.japanese: {面接官|めんせつかん}は{三人|さんにん}いて、それぞれ{違|ちが}う{角度|かくど}から{質問|しつもん}してきた。
examples.english: There were three interviewers, and each asked questions from a different angle.

notes:
USAGE:
The {官|かん} suffix indicates a person in an official role. Used in job interview and university entrance exam contexts. The person being interviewed is {面接者|めんせつしゃ} or {受験者|じゅけんしゃ}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {面接官|めんせつかん}の{質問|しつもん} (interviewer's question)
- {面接官|めんせつかん}に{好印象|こういんしょう}を{与|あた}える (to make a good impression on the interviewer)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {試験官|しけんかん}: examiner — for written or practical exams
- {審査員|しんさいん}: judge, evaluator — broader judging contexts
